name: tactical_transition_independent_v1
notes: Frozen V2 prospective evaluation; 32 human-authored adversarial examples across four FA resources. Excerpts are selected passages, not full documents. Gold labels need independent review for deployment qualification. Do not tune on these cases before first run.

cases.claim: La transizione comprende la risposta immediata alla perdita o al recupero del possesso.
cases.evidence: Transition is the process of recognition and response in the first few moments following the regaining or loss of possession. Responding quickly and intelligently to a changeover in possession, will allow England teams to exploit attacking opportunities and effectively re-organise defensively when out of possession. Once the player in possession (or the player closest to the ball in defensive transition) makes a decision, the supporting units and the rest of the team must support the initial movement for transition to be effective. The goalkeeper plays a key role in transition by exploiting opportunities to begin attacking moves as well as positioning, organising and communicating effectively during defensive transition.
cases.source_title: The FA — England DNA: Transition

cases.claim: Nell'esempio inglese i difensori centrali avanzano per sostenere l'attacco, ma arretrano rapidamente dopo la perdita del pallone.
cases.evidence: When transition happens, teams are vulnerable. The opposition will exploit whatever space is available. To prevent this, your players need to be comfortable defending in central and wide areas to successfully delay and deny their attacks. England's central defenders push up high to support the attack. This helps them to support the attack by retaining the ball and puts them in a great position to counter press in moments of transition when possession is lost. A key part of England’s out of possession strategy is to be compact within the centre of the pitch and force the opposition out wide. The three England central defenders deny the space behind them by turning and sprinting back to their own half. This tactic forces the Iceland goalkeeper to throw the ball wide and gives the rest of the team more time to make recovery runs. Smaller areas result in more transitions and opportunities to counter press. Larger areas allow players to experience tracking back over bigger distances and getting into shape as they quickly change from attack to defence.
cases.source_title: The FA — How to defend like England: transition

cases.claim: La preparazione della transizione inizia anche prima che cambi il possesso.
cases.evidence: Transition is defined as the reaction and response, individually and collectively, to the first few moments between having the ball or not having the ball. Crucially, whatever the first response is to the transition, an individual must be backed up by those around them. For example, if a centre forward goes to press a defender, then they need support from behind. Likewise, an attacker who decides to counter needs supporting runs from others. When possession is lost a team can become extremely vulnerable. Players need to develop their ability to react effectively and think about transition before the ball has changed hands. Emotional control and decision-making are important aspects of successful transitions. Players should know in advance what options they have before possession is regained. Decision-making in transition can be improved by recreating relevant scenarios in training.
cases.source_title: The FA — How to coach transition

cases.claim: La sicurezza difensiva va considerata anche mentre la squadra è in possesso.
cases.evidence: England DNA Principles – Transition: Defending the Counter Attack. During all aspects of the in-possession philosophy, defensive security should be considered. Awareness of defensive security ensures the team remains organised at all times and can react effectively when the ball is lost. All players contribute to ensuring defensive security, in particular the goalkeeper through effective positioning, organisation and communication.
